absent: Locking, concurrency and sleep context rules for socket buffers, splice descriptors and backplane register access.
State machines for socket creation and teardown, splice pipe progress and backplane enumeration.
Implementations behind user copy, pipe buffer operations, splice range primitive and bus read write methods.
Selection rule deciding which compatibility fixup form is built and how fixups are applied.

findings.text: Socket address families form a dense integer namespace from zero for unspecified through forty five for management component transport, with forty six as exclusive upper bound. Value one is shared by Unix and local names. Value sixteen is shared by netlink and route names. Other values separate internet versions four and six, packet, radio, telecom, wireless, virtual and accelerator families.

Protocol family identifiers numerically mirror address family identifiers one to one, with each protocol value defined equal to its address counterpart and sharing the same upper bound, so either namespace can be used interchangeably where a family number is expected.
The largest backlog value a listener may request is four thousand ninety six, serving as a clamp for user supplied queue lengths.

Message control flags are powers of two with assignments MSG_OOB 1, MSG_PEEK 2, MSG_DONTROUTE 4, MSG_CTRUNC 8, MSG_PROBE 16, MSG_TRUNC 32, MSG_DONTWAIT 64, MSG_EOR 128, MSG_WAITALL 256, MSG_FIN 512, MSG_SYN 1024, MSG_CONFIRM 2048, MSG_RST 4096, MSG_ERRQUEUE 8192, MSG_NOSIGNAL 16384, MSG_MORE 32768, MSG_WAITFORONE 65536, MSG_BATCH 262144, MSG_NO_SHARED_FRAGS 524288, MSG_SENDPAGE_DECRYPTED 1048576, MSG_SOCK_DEVMEM 33554432, MSG_ZEROCOPY 67108864, MSG_SPLICE_PAGES 134217728, MSG_FASTOPEN 536870912 and MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC 1073741824. MSG_TRYHARD aliases MSG_DONTROUTE, MSG_EOF aliases MSG_FIN, and MSG_SENDPAGE_NOPOLICY shares the WAITFORONE value with meaning chosen by call path.

Control compatibility marker is build dependent, either top bit set when thirty two bit fixups may be needed or zero when they never occur. Internal send mask combines splice pages, no policy, decrypted content and unshared fragment markers to identify kernel only bits that must be stripped from user visible flag sets.

Option levels use SOL_IP 0, SOL_TCP 6, SOL_UDP 17, SOL_IPV6 41, SOL_ICMPV6 58, SOL_SCTP 132, SOL_UDPLITE 136 and SOL_RAW 255, followed by a dense block SOL_IPX 256 through SOL_VSOCK 287 covering legacy, ATM, wireless, multimedia and modern transports. IPX type marker is value one.

Splice flags use bit zero for move, bit one for nonblock, bit two for more, bit three for gift, with decimal values one, two, four and eight. Aggregate mask combines all four. Move prefers page transfer, nonblock avoids pipe blocking, more predicts further input, gift passes page ownership to the pipe.

Backplane core types use values hexadecimal 800 for chipcommon through 82A for ARM Cortex M3, with intermediate values for memory controllers, interconnects, Ethernet, wireless, USB, storage and application processors. Vendor code for Broadcom is hexadecimal 4243.

Internal timestamping state is a fixed array of three kernel time values used to carry staged hardware or software capture moments through the stack, separate from user exposed timestamp representations.

Tagged socket pointer overlays kernel and user addresses in a union with a one bit discriminant. When the tag indicates kernel, the kernel member is valid, otherwise the user member is valid. This allows a single handle to pass option buffers from either domain.

Splice progress record keeps remaining byte total, current segment length and flag word, destination context, completion handling and position state. Destination context is a union selecting user memory, file handle or opaque cookie. Position state pairs a direct offset with an optional output offset pointer, plus moved byte count, unexpected end callback and writer wakeup request.
Partial page record stores offset and length inside one page together with a private word for pipe or allocator bookkeeping, allowing a page vector to describe scattered or short spans.

Pipe splice vector groups page pointers with parallel partial metadata, populated count, array capacity, output pipe operations and a release callback. Associated actor callbacks consume pipe buffers or drive direct pipe to pipe movement and report status as integer.
Per radio core power record holds idle targets and maxima for low and high bands plus four element amplifier tables for each sub band, encoding factory calibration for transmit power control.

Backplane PROM cache is a large flat device description with revision, four hardware addresses, transceiver wiring, device and board identity, country indication, LED timing, antenna availability, legacy amplifier words, general purpose lines, band maxima, idle targets, isolation, per antenna indexes, receive offsets, signal strength tuning, CCK and OFDM offsets, board flag words in legacy split and modern combined forms, four embedded per core power records, antenna gains, front end tuning for low and high bands, modulation offsets, gain error and noise tables, chain selection, temperature compensation, per rate power tables and SAR limits.
Board identity pairs sixteen bit vendor and type codes used to select platform specific configuration.

Bus method table abstracts register access by width with byte, half word and word readers and writers addressed by device and offset. When block transfer support is configured, additional block read and write methods move counted buffers with register width selection.

Constructors lift a raw kernel address or a user address into the tagged handle with the domain bit set accordingly. Null test inspects only the active union member. Offset copy from tagged source into kernel destination dispatches to user aware copy for user handles and plain memory copy for kernel handles, honoring a byte offset.

Inbound copy family moves from tagged source to kernel buffer. Plain form copies from start. Safe form requires caller length at least expected size before copying fixed length and reports invalid length or access failure distinctly. Struct form negotiates differing caller and kernel sizes through user or bounce buffer struct copy depending on tag.

Outbound copy family moves from kernel source to tagged destination. Plain form writes from start. Struct form negotiates caller and kernel sizes and optionally reports whether nonzero trailing source bytes were ignored, selecting user or bounce buffer implementation by destination tag.

Kernel bounce struct copy checks caller size against known object size, copies the common prefix of source and destination sizes, clears excess destination bytes when destination is larger, and flags cases where a smaller destination would discard nonzero trailing source bytes. Callers translate ignored trailing bytes or oversize requests into too big errors.

Duplication helpers allocate fresh kernel memory then copy tagged content into it, encoding allocation failure as out of memory and copy failure as fault after freeing. Null terminated variant reserves one extra byte and appends zero. Bounded string copy measures kernel strings within count and delegates user strings to user aware copy. Zero verification scans a tagged range for any nonzero byte using user or memory scan by tag.

File range copy adapter forwards input file with input offset, output file with output offset and byte length to the reference based splice range primitive, converting value based offsets into the pointer form expected downstream.

Single inclusion guards protect socket pointer, splice and backplane headers. Protocol numbers equal address numbers. Unix aliases local, route aliases netlink, tryhard aliases dontroute and end marker aliases finish. Shared value between wait for one and internal no policy marker requires interpretation by entry point rather than numeric value alone.

Tagged helpers use zero for success, negative invalid argument when caller length is too small, negative fault when user access fails, negative too big when struct size negotiation would expose or discard unexpected bytes or exceed known object size, negative out of memory on allocation failure, and encoded error pointers for failed duplication. Null checks never fault.

Kernel only send markers, zero copy, device memory, splice pages and decrypted page flags change buffer ownership, lifetime or encryption expectations and must be masked before exposing flags to user space or reusing pages. Compatibility marker changes control message fixup handling by build. Splice move and gift transfer page ownership so callers must not retain source pages after success.

Block read and write members of the backplane operation table exist only when block input output support is enabled. Code that dereferences them without that configuration will fail to build or will read an absent member, so drivers must use width specific accessors or guard block paths.
